search_log: Searched "Jojo Moyes After You excerpt first chapter publisher" and opened the sustained Booktopia/Penguin-branded Chapter One extract.
Searched "After You Jojo Moyes first person narrator point of view" and opened BookRags' explicit whole-book style description.
Searched "After You exception of one chapter Louisa" and "After You Chapter 19 narrator"; the Penguin Random House reader's guide identified the Lily perspective shift.
Searched "Chapter 19 Lily After You Jojo Moyes perspective third person"; SuperSummary explicitly identified Chapter 19 as the sole third-person chapter.
Checked Google Books and publisher product pages; their catalog descriptions verified the edition but did not independently expose enough Chapter 19 prose to establish grammatical person.
person_note: The sampled quotations overwhelmingly expose Louisa Clark's participating first-person base narration, while dialogue, aphorisms, and generic uses of you are nondiagnostic. The sample contains no passage from the structural exception. Web research resolves that gap: an authorized opening confirms Louisa's sustained first person, and multiple structural sources identify Chapter 19 as a sustained Lily section; the explicit structural analysis and interior text establish that this chapter is third person. Because the methodology assigns ALTERNATING whenever sustained sections use different persons, the single full third-person chapter makes the book ALTERNATING rather than simply FIRST. The only minor limitation is that the official publisher guide names the perspective shift without itself naming its grammatical person, but independent whole-book analysis and chapter text resolve that point.
